subject: Candidate WVB 1.39 borrowed identity across direct calls
claim: The focused Windows publication selection passed 39 cases in 15,345 ms warm. Exact borrowed parameter and argument metadata survives direct forwarding, earlier bytecode remains unchanged, and large borrow-free functions retain their prior limits. This is source-publication evidence, not WVB 1.39 runtime admission.

source.value: Worktree based on 3c781190b8260e481910e19b09e8c463c6092f47. Final writer and verifier inputs are identified below. The source writer's borrow-free guard was corrected before its analysis snapshot and native emitter construction. The first successful cold run used the preceding 113,711-byte owner runner (SHA-256 bff78d4995ff80d1bb93401888cfe62b8621419660b439fd11b4ae6d95734ca8); the final runner adds two large-function regressions and streamed child progress without changing compiler inputs. Output names identify temporary products, not committed release artifacts.

runs.target: Approved one-hour publication check: 37 cases, including missing native compiler package construction. Pinned analyzer and several project WVB products were already cached.
Expanded selection: borrowing cases passed, but the first large standalone fixture incorrectly supplied unused library modules and was rejected by source-graph admission before emission.

Final 39-case selection with corrected fixture dependencies: native planner 16, structural publication 20, large borrow-free regressions 2, unchanged earlier bytecode 1. All compiler products were cache hits; source fixtures were compiled and behavior checked afresh.

runs.host: Local Windows x64; PowerShell 7 and Node.js 24.19.0
runs.target: Final routing and framework checks: 31 general cases, 280 native cases, positive and excluded planner selections, development dependencies, and shared command fault checks
Final documentation: 1,587 Markdown files, 5,694 links, 462 anchors, 14 retrieval cases, and current catalogs

limitations: Windows development evidence only. No Linux reproduction, clean-machine bootstrap, independent reproduction, complete 210-case owner, or broad qualification was run.

The complete compiler-aligned verifier, scalar runtime, native lowerer, WebAssembly, package, and OS consumers still reject WVB 1.39. The native execution here is the planner self-test, not execution of candidate borrowed payload bytecode.

The structural reader checks six functions, four types, three E1 instructions, three borrowed Option-view locals, twenty borrowed-payload local/parameter shapes, and eight direct calls. It is bounded to 16 MiB and is not a complete typed-stack or lifetime verifier.

The direct-call fixture covers nominal records and u32, plain-owner arguments, and borrowed forwarding. It does not qualify arbitrary payload types, indirect calls, exclusive borrowing, take, mapping, or consumer migration.

The large-function workload uses 1,100 assignments and retains 50,636 code bytes with 3,303 local slots. Standalone bytes match the pinned emitter. The mixed module compiled successfully but was not executed.

Cold and warm observations use different case counts because two regression cases were added after the initial build. They measure content-keyed product reuse, not a like-for-like compiler algorithm speedup. No stable performance threshold or complete process-tree peak-memory measurement is claimed.
The earlier approved twenty-minute interruption remains incomplete evidence in the separate planner record. Completed caches were reused; partial products were not treated as passing.
